title: About the Craftsman
paragraphs: People often ask how I got started making handcrafted walking canes, and the truth is, it wasn't something I ever planned.

Several years ago, I suffered a serious back injury while preventing a bariatric patient from hurting themselves. After multiple back surgeries, I found myself relying on a walking cane every day. Like many people, I began looking for something that was both dependable and meaningful.
That's when I found an Irish shillelagh.

There was something special about it. It wasn't just another walking cane; it had character. The natural wood grain, the craftsmanship, and the feeling that someone had taken the time to create it by hand really stuck with me. It reminded me that something practical could also be beautiful.
That experience inspired me to start making my own.

What began as a hobby quickly became a passion. I started learning about different hardwoods, experimenting with techniques, and spending countless hours in the workshop. I discovered that every piece of wood has its own personality. The grain, color, knots, and curves all help tell the story of the finished cane.

Today, I build each cane by hand using locally sourced hardwood whenever possible. No two pieces of wood are exactly alike, which means no two canes are either. Every cane is shaped, sanded, and finished with care, taking the time to let the natural beauty of the wood shine through.
Whether you're looking for dependable everyday support, a meaningful gift, or a one-of-a-kind custom piece, I hope you find something here that speaks to you.

Thank you for visiting my workshop and supporting handcrafted craftsmanship. It truly means a great deal to me, and I hope one of these canes becomes something you'll be proud to carry for years to come.
